items.title: All sources reach ExoPlayer as plain MPEG-TS over the loopback RelayBridge
items.facts: Dart owns every network protocol (:8800 Digest+multipart+AES, relay TLS tunnel, optional RTSP). It emits plain video/mp2t bytes on http://127.0.0.1:<port>/camera/<id>.ts?k=<per-launch key>. ExoPlayer (ProgressiveMediaSource + DefaultExtractorsFactory TS flags) only ever sees one unbounded HTTP TS file. Keep the existing RelayBridge key check (24 chars from Random.secure), 404 on bad key/path, 502 with lastErrors[deviceId] when no first bytes, bufferOutput=false, Content-Type video/mp2t, Cache-Control no-store. Generalise _resolve to return a MediaSource (local8800 | relay | rtsp) exposing Stream<Uint8List> openTs().

items.title: Local :8800 handshake: unauthenticated POST, 401 Digest retry, Key-Exchange
items.facts: Open TCP (NODELAY) to <ip>:8800. Send 'POST /stream HTTP/1.1' with headers in order Host, Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=--client-stream-boundary--, Connection: keep-alive, Content-Length: 0, X-Key-Exchange: 1, then Authorization on retry. 401 -> parse WWW-Authenticate (realm, qop, nonce, opaque, algorithm, encrypt_type, userhash). If response Connection: close, reopen socket before retry. Secret = SHA256_HEX_UPPER(secret) when encrypt_type==3 else MD5_HEX_UPPER; secret is the LAT when known else the cloud password; empty -> default media password. Digest username admin, uri /stream, nc 00000001, qop first token, no spaces between fields. Second 401 -> auth failure, never retry (lockout rule). HTTP 503 / -52407 -> stream limit. After 200 read Key-Exchange header (space separated k=v, quotes stripped, nonce required).

items.title: Legacy MD5 stream key and IV
items.facts: Key-Exchange without algorithm=HKDF: key = MD5(nonce + ':' + secret) raw 16 bytes, iv = MD5(username + ':' + nonce) raw 16 bytes, AES-128-CBC PKCS7, fixed IV reused for every part (fresh cipher per part). username admin -> secret is the transformed (UPPER hex) password; username none -> default media password (untransformed); any other username -> no key, parts cannot be read.

items.title: HKDF stream keys, X-Nonce IV and X-Data-Hmac check
items.facts: Key-Exchange algorithm=HKDF (C200 fw 1.5.7): ikm = nonce + ':' + secret (secret = SHA256_HEX_UPPER of the LAT or password), salt = Key-Exchange 'salt' as UTF-8 bytes (None when empty), HKDF-SHA256 L=16, info 'stream_hkdf_aes_key' and 'stream_hkdf_hmac_key'. Per part: iv = hex-decode(X-Nonce) must be 16 bytes; X-Data-Hmac (optional) = base64(HMAC-SHA256(hmac_key, ciphertext)) compared in constant time; then AES-128-CBC PKCS7. Bad part is dropped (not fatal); >50 consecutive failures raise a broken-session error. Only parts with X-If-Encrypt: 1 are decrypted. Dart: package:cryptography or pointycastle (HKDF, AES-CBC); for 2-4 Mbit/s TS prefer a Kotlin MethodChannel/isolate only if Dart AES profiling shows >30% CPU on a TV box (open question).

items.title: Multipart framing: device parts in, client parts out
items.facts: Device boundary line on the wire is '--' + '--device-stream-boundary--' (four hyphens); client likewise '----client-stream-boundary--'. Parser: skip lines until one equals the delimiter, read header block to CRLFCRLF (latin-1, name: value), require numeric Content-Length (max part 16 MiB), then exactly that many body bytes; ignore blank/junk/closing lines; header block cap 64 KiB. Client parts: delimiter line, extra headers in insertion order, Content-Type, Content-Length, blank line, body, CRLF. JSON control bodies are compact (separators ',' ':'), seq starts at 1; X-Session-Id added automatically once known. The existing Dart parseRelayResponse uses containment matching and no pending-state buffering; replace it with a stateful MultipartReader shared by local and relay.

items.title: Preview request, session_id, acks, stop with linger
items.facts: After connect send {type:request,params:{method:get,preview:{channels:[0],resolutions:[HD|VGA],audio:[default]}}} (seq added = 1). HD = main stream, VGA = minor stream. Wait for type=response with matching seq (or none); result.error_code in {-52407,-52405,-52419,-52435} = fatal stream-limit, other non-zero = refused. Media parts (video/mp2t) that arrive before the response are kept (max 8) and replayed. session_id is read from params.session_id (real cameras) or result.session_id, or the X-Session-Id header; without it no ack/stop is sent. Ack every 25th X-Data-Sequence: part with X-Data-Received then X-Session-Id headers. Skip parts with Content-Type audio/*. End notifications: connection_closed, stream_finish, device_locked, internal_error; type=error ends the pump. Stop: send {type:request,params:{method:do,stop:null-string 'null'}} then wait 150 ms BEFORE closing the socket (Windows RST dropped the stop; apply the same linger on Android to be safe), then close. Backpressure: write to the HTTP response and await it; do not queue unboundedly. I/O timeout max(3 s, stall+1). Stall watchdog 5 s, backoff 0.5 s doubling to 10 s, TCP reachability probe 3 s before handshake.

items.title: Relay slot request (cloudType 2) and CIPC headers
items.facts: POST https://<cipc>/v2/relay/request, cipc from getAppServiceUrl serviceId cipc.api.cloud, fallback aps1-cipc-api.i.tplinkcloud.com. Authorization = raw account token before ';' (no ut|, not signed). Headers: Content-Type application/json; charset=UTF-8, Accept */*, User-Agent Tapo_APP/<model>/<ver>_Android/Android 14, X-Request-Signature 10 random alnum, X-Client-Id terminal uuid, X-Source tapo-app, X-Brand TPLINK, X-Ca-Type cloud-self, Connection close. Body compact JSON: deviceId, dataTimeoutCount 0, cloudType 2 (1 only when device list says isSupportIoTCloud false), deviceType SMART.IPCAMERA, playerId, rootCaVer '1', then preConnection 0, resolution HD|VGA, streamType 0, customParams '{}', trackId uuid4. -1102/HTTP 401 -> one silent re-login then retry once. Fatal codes: -1007 camera offline, -1103 not bound, -52407, -52212, -100001, -20675, 3. TV baseline already sends cloudType 2 (tapo_cloud.dart:550); verify body key set against Windows.

items.title: Relay tunnel request: exact header order
items.facts: TLS to relayIp:443 (fallback relay host), SNI/hostname check = relay host from relayUrl, TCP_NODELAY, trust TP-Link roots plus system. Send one never-ending 'POST <relayPath>&retryTime=0 HTTP/1.1' (use ? if path has no query) with headers in this exact order: User-Agent 'Client=TP-Link_Tapo_Android Android <ver>/1.3', Keep-Relay 3600, Accept */*, Content-Type multipart/mixed;boundary=--client-stream-boundary--, Host, Content-Length 9223372036854775807, X-token, X-Client-Model, X-Client-UUID, X-Track-Id, X-Redirect-Times, X-Pull-Mode 2, [Cookie ELB], X-Version 2.0, X-Arrive-Latency (TCP connect ms). Missing X-Version gives 400 errorCode 3 illegal_request. Read the response head byte-by-byte so nothing after 200 is consumed. 200 -> raw tunnel. 304 -> body is RequestUrlResult, reconnect with X-Redirect-Times+1 (max 3). Other -> JSON errorCode/closeReason. TV baseline differs: Host first, no X-Track-Id, extra Connection: Keep-alive, X-Redirect-Times fixed at 0, Cookie placed last. Align to the Windows order and add 304 handling.

items.title: Relay media session: preview request, heartbeat every 15 s, plain TS
items.facts: Inside the tunnel there is no inner POST /stream and no Digest. The client writes the same preview request part as on LAN (resolution = slot resolution) and then reads device parts. A heartbeat part is written every 15 s: body is exactly '{"type": "notification", "params": {"event_type": "heartbeat"}}' (with spaces, 63 bytes), encoded as a client part. Reader and writer share one TLS socket: serialise writes (Dart SecureSocket.add is safe from one isolate, so run heartbeat on the same isolate and flush). Fresh slot + tunnel on every (re)connect (relayToken is single use). Acks use the same session_id logic as LAN. The TV baseline does NOT send the preview request or heartbeat; add both. Windows treats X-If-Encrypt:1 on a relay part as an error and the TV baseline throws too. If a relay part has X-If-Encrypt:1 and no Key-Exchange was received, report 'relay encrypted media' with part headers (names only) so a live capture can decide the key schedule.

items.title: Encrypted relay parts (new work on TV)
items.facts: The Windows app and spec treat relay media as plaintext; no live capture shows X-If-Encrypt:1 on relay. The brief lists encrypted relay parts as new TV work. Design: MultipartReader surfaces X-If-Encrypt/X-Nonce/X-Data-Hmac; a PartDecryptor interface with implementations Hkdf (needs Key-Exchange salt/nonce), Md5, and Passthrough. Relay has no Key-Exchange header (spec), so a key cannot be derived unless the camera/cloud supplies one later; until a capture proves otherwise, relay uses Passthrough and fails clearly on X-If-Encrypt:1 instead of feeding ciphertext to ExoPlayer.

items.title: TV baseline vs Windows: relay gaps to close
items.facts: Baseline RelayBridge/openVideoStream: (1) no preview JSON request and no heartbeat after tunnel open; (2) tunnel header order and set differ (Host first, no X-Track-Id, Connection: Keep-alive added, hard-coded X-Redirect-Times 0, no 304 follow); (3) no session_id/ack handling; (4) parseRelayResponse matches the boundary by containment and relies on readExact, no JSON-part handling, and it never checks Content-Type, so every part body including JSON control parts is emitted as video; (5) throws on X-If-Encrypt; (6) no stop request on close (socket.destroy only). Keep: loopback bridge, per-launch key, first-bytes-before-200 error mapping, StreamQueue, snapshots, latency watch.

items.title: ExoPlayer configuration for the loopback TS file
items.facts: Keep LivePlayer.kt: ProgressiveMediaSource + DefaultHttpDataSource (connect 10 s, read 30 s) over DefaultExtractorsFactory with TS flags FLAG_ALLOW_NON_IDR_KEYFRAMES | FLAG_DETECT_ACCESS_UNITS (camera TS has no IDR-aligned starts and no AUD), DefaultLoadControl.setBufferDurationsMs(500, 4000, 250, 500) with prioritizeTime, TextureView, volume 0 (until audio exists). Live-edge catch-up: 1.25x speed while buffered-ahead > 1500 ms, back to 1x under 600 ms. Because the bridge only answers after the first TS bytes, a source failure becomes an HTTP 502 and ExoPlayer raises onPlayerError; Dart maps lastErrors[deviceId] to the UI. Local :8800 VGA/HD and relay share the same view; the camera may start mid-GOP so first frame needs the next keyframe (stall timer 5 s, give-up 25 s in live_player.dart).

items.title: Focus-less native view and emulator software decoder
items.facts: LiveVideoView: TextureView isFocusable=false, isFocusableInTouchMode=false, importantForAccessibility NO; Flutter side wraps in ExcludeFocus with PlatformViewHitTestBehavior.transparent and initExpensiveAndroidView (hybrid composition) so D-pad focus stays in Flutter. Emulator detection: HARDWARE contains goldfish or ranchu, PRODUCT starts with sdk_, FINGERPRINT contains generic; there MediaCodecSelector sorts decoders software-first (goldfish HW H.264 decoder stalls after about a dozen live frames). Real TVs keep hardware decoders; setEnableDecoderFallback(true). Windows analogue: grid tiles software, fullscreen HD hardware (stream_policy.decoder_for): on TV keep HW for all unless many simultaneous tiles exhaust codec instances (see mb.policy.codec_budget).

items.title: ExoPlayer cannot play G.711 A-law inside MPEG-TS
items.facts: media3 DefaultTsPayloadReaderFactory creates payload readers only for stream types MPA 0x03/0x04, AAC ADTS 0x0F, AAC LATM 0x11, AC-3 0x81, E-AC-3 0x87, AC-4 0xAC, DTS 0x8A/0x82/0x88/0x8B, MPEG-2/H.263/H.264/H.265 video, ID3 0x15, SCTE 0x86, DVB subs 0x59. There is no G.711 reader; an unknown stream type (G.711 A-law is PMT stream_type 0x90 on Tapo cameras per pytapo/go2rtc) yields no track and the audio is silently dropped. So a camera TS with pcm_alaw plays video only and does not break playback. Remuxing inside TS cannot help because media3 has no PCM-in-TS reader either.
tests: test/media/ts_audio_probe_test.dart: PMT with stream_type 0x90 is detected as alaw

items.title: Audio design: Dart strips A-law PES, decodes to PCM16, plays via AudioTrack
items.facts: Phase 1 (P0): leave audio in the TS (ExoPlayer ignores it), player.volume stays 0, no work. Phase 2 (P1/P2): a TsAudioTap in Dart walks 188-byte TS packets, parses PAT/PMT, finds the audio PID (stream_type 0x90 = A-law, or 0x0F AAC which ExoPlayer plays natively with no tap), reassembles PES payloads (8 kHz mono, 1 byte per sample), decodes with the 256-entry A-law table to s16le and sends PCM chunks over a MethodChannel/EventChannel to a Kotlin AudioTrack (8000 Hz, mono, ENCODING_PCM_16BIT, MODE_STREAM, small buffer). The tap runs only for the focused/fullscreen camera and a mute toggle defaults to muted; sync with video is approximate (PTS offset) which is acceptable for monitoring. Alternative considered: have Kotlin MediaCodec 'audio/g711-alaw' decode - rejected because ExoPlayer still would not demux it from TS. Windows never decoded live audio (AGENTS.md: audio in live view not built); alaw.py is only a reference table.

items.title: Per-camera concurrent stream limit = 2
items.facts: The camera accepts at most 2 concurrent media sessions (RTSP 2 per firmware; :8800 live and playback share the same 2, limiter key = host). StreamLimiter: thread-safe counter per key, acquire(host, timeout) raises StreamLimitError, lease released idempotently. Camera refusal arrives as error_code -52407/-52405/-52419/-52435 or HTTP 503 and is FATAL (no retry loop). Relay streams use the cloud deviceId as limiter key. Dart port: a StreamLimiter keyed by camera id with max 2, acquired before opening any source, released in finally; live + SD playback of the same camera count against the same limiter. Grid tile + fullscreen of the same camera must reuse or hand over the one stream (switch resolution in place, keep the lease).

items.title: Remote relay gate: max remote streams, reserved view slots
items.facts: RemoteStreamGate: capacity = setting max_remote_streams (1..16, default 4); acquire(key, on_evict, preempt) evicts the oldest holder when full; reserve(keys) gives every camera in the current view a guaranteed slot (holders may exceed capacity, never evicted). Windows measured 11 relay streams at about 6-7 fps each vs 17 fps for one. On TV, with hardware codec limits, default capacity 4 relay streams outside the view; view-reserved cameras always stream. Gate lives in Dart, keyed by camera id.

items.title: Staggered start of streams
items.facts: Windows has no staggering (open item: 8-10 s to first frame when 11 relays start at once). TV baseline StreamQueue allows 1 connecting stream at a time, hands the slot on at first frame, failure, dispose or after 5 s (slotTimeout), and Retry bypasses the queue. Keep it. Extend: slot also gates the :8800 handshake (Digest) and relay slot request, not only ExoPlayer start; never start two local streams to one camera at once (limit 2 includes ghost sessions from a not-yet-closed previous one, hence the 150 ms stop linger). Give-up after 25 s with manual Retry; auto-retry backoff 2 s x failures.

items.title: Quality policy and codec budget on TV
items.facts: Windows: every camera in a visible grid slot streams; grid uses VGA (minor stream, 640x360 decode), fullscreen uses HD (main) and only that camera streams; decode sizes fixed per quality so resizing never restarts; grid = software decode (38 MB vs 110 MB per process) fullscreen = hardware. TV: no ffmpeg, ExoPlayer instance per tile. Android TV chips typically allow 2-4 concurrent HW H.264 decoders; recommend: grid tiles VGA, max visible tiles per page = 4 (grid <=2x2) unless the device passes a codec-capacity probe; fullscreen switches the same camera to HD by restarting the preview (switch keeps the limiter lease). Local resolution selection via preview resolutions VGA/HD; relay via slot resolution.

items.title: Loopback bridge security
items.facts: Bind HttpServer to 127.0.0.1 port 0 only; require per-launch random key k on every URL, 404 otherwise; never log URLs with k; strip secrets (LAT, password, relay token, ELB cookie) from lastErrors and exceptions (Windows _hide/redact_url); one-shot relayToken; no cleartext traffic exemption beyond 127.0.0.1 in the network security config (Android 9+ blocks http by default: add a domain-config for 127.0.0.1 only). Camera IPs and ids never in logs or fixtures (use 192.168.1.x).

decisions.decision: Dart terminates every protocol (Digest, Key-Exchange, AES/HKDF, multipart, relay TLS tunnel, acks, heartbeat, stop) and exposes only plain video/mp2t on the 127.0.0.1 RelayBridge with the per-launch key. No Kotlin networking, no ffmpeg. One MediaSource interface (local8800, relay, later vod) feeds the same bridge route /camera/<id>.ts.
Never forward JSON, audio/* or undecryptable parts to ExoPlayer: only video/mp2t bodies after HMAC check and decrypt; dropped bad parts do not end the stream (>50 consecutive does).

Audio: ExoPlayer/TsExtractor has no G.711 reader, so pcm_alaw (TS stream_type 0x90) is silently ignored and no remux inside TS can make it playable. P0 ships video only (volume 0). P2 adds a Dart TsAudioTap + A-law table decode + native AudioTrack for the focused camera, muted by default. AAC cameras play in ExoPlayer natively.

Per-camera limit 2 concurrent sessions via StreamLimiter keyed by camera id (local host or cloud deviceId); limit errors are fatal. Staggered start via existing StreamQueue (1 connecting at a time, 5 s slot timeout) extended to cover handshake and slot request.

Relay: align tunnel header order/set with Windows, add preview request, 15 s heartbeat, session_id acks (every 25th X-Data-Sequence), stop with 150 ms linger, 304 redirect follow (max 3), fresh slot per attempt. Encrypted relay parts stay unsupported (clear error) until a live capture defines the key schedule.

Keep LivePlayer.kt as is for P0: TS extractor flags, small LoadControl, 1.25x catch-up, TextureView non-focusable, emulator software-decoder preference. RTSP (P2) uses media3 RtspMediaSource natively, not the bridge.

Golden vectors for HKDF/MD5/HMAC/framing/A-law hex values were computed from the Windows implementation (python importing tapo_desktop read-only) because the Windows tests assert them structurally; the TV tests must pin these literals.

open_questions.question: Does the relay ever send X-If-Encrypt:1 parts, and with which key schedule (no Key-Exchange header exists in the tunnel)? Needs a live capture by the owner (headers only, no payload stored).

Dart AES-CBC + HMAC throughput on low-end Android TV SoCs for 2-4 Mbit/s HD streams on :8800; is a Kotlin (javax.crypto) decrypt via EventChannel or a background isolate needed? Benchmark before choosing.
How many concurrent hardware H.264 decoders do target TVs allow, and what max grid size is safe? Needs MediaCodecList probing (getMaxSupportedInstances) or an on-device test.
Does media3 RTSP handle PCMA audio (RtpPcmReader) and Tapo /stream1 auth (Digest) on the pinned media3 version? Verify before the P2 RTSP item.
Is the PMT stream_type for Tapo A-law really 0x90 on :8800 and relay TS (spec says external: pytapo/go2rtc)? Verify with a sample capture before writing TsAudioTap.
Does ExoPlayer start cleanly when the TS begins mid-GOP on :8800 (first frame after the next keyframe), and is the 25 s give-up in live_player.dart enough for relay cold starts?
Windows spec confidence for remote.relay.stream_over_tunnel is 'inferred' for the inner flow; the 304 redirect and X-Track-Id requirements are verified on hardware only for cloudType 2 cameras.
